CONTEXT.content: Every database query costs time and money. Caching stores frequently accessed data in fast memory so you don't recompute or re-fetch it. But caches introduce a new problem: stale data.
CONTEXT.analogy: A cache is like keeping yesterday's newspaper on your desk — fast to read, but it might be outdated.
CONTEXT.productionNote: Cache invalidation is one of the two hard problems in computer science. Getting it wrong causes subtle bugs that only appear under load.
hints: What data in your URL shortener is read more than written?

DECIDE.optionA: Cache-aside: app checks cache first, falls back to DB, writes to cache on miss.
DECIDE.optionB: Write-through: every write goes to cache AND database simultaneously.

tradeoffs.A: Simpler invalidation; cache miss penalty on first read.
tradeoffs.B: Always fresh on read; write latency increases, cache and DB can diverge on failure.

hints: Consider read-heavy vs write-heavy patterns for URL lookups.

BUILD.goal: Add an in-memory cache to your URL shortener's lookup path. Cache hits should skip the database.

tracks.node: Use a Map or node-cache. Add cache hit/miss logging.
tracks.python: Use functools.lru_cache or a dict with TTL.
tracks.go: Use sync.Map or a simple map with mutex.
tracks.typescript: Use Map with optional TTL tracking.

acceptance: First lookup hits DB, subsequent lookups hit cache (prove with logs)
Cache miss falls back to DB correctly
New links are findable after creation (no stale miss)
hints: Log 'cache hit' vs 'cache miss' to prove it's working.
What happens when a link is updated?

criteria: Show logs proving cache hit on second request
Show cache miss after creating a new link
hints: Verification needs log output, not just 'it feels faster'.

BREAK.scenario: After a deploy, users report old redirect URLs for recently updated links.
BREAK.symptoms: Database has correct URL. Cache serves old URL. Restarting fixes it temporarily.
hints: When does the cache get updated vs the database?
Is there a TTL? Should there be?

FIX.goal: Fix cache invalidation so updates are reflected immediately.
hints: On write, what should happen to the cache entry?
Cache-aside pattern: invalidate on write, not just on TTL expiry.

decisionCallbacks.A: Cache-aside made invalidation your responsibility — the bug was a missing invalidation on write.
decisionCallbacks.B: Write-through would have kept cache fresh but the failure mode when cache write fails is its own lesson.
